subject: Civil Engineering
title: Irregularity in Plan and Elevation
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Irregularity in Plan and Elevation.

hook.text: Symmetric buildings ride earthquakes like a boat on waves. Irregular ones twist and fail.

buildup.text: Plan irregularity — L-shapes, T-shapes — causes torsion. One wing twists against another.

discovery.text: Vertical irregularity — setbacks, soft stories — concentrates damage at the transition.

twist.text: Seismic joints separate irregular buildings into regular blocks — each sways independently.

climax.text: Codes penalize irregular buildings with higher design forces — a built-in safety margin.

punchline.text: Simple, symmetric shapes survive earthquakes best. Complexity invites failure.

quiz.question: What problem does plan irregularity cause during an earthquake?
options: The building sinks unevenly into the soil
Asymmetric stiffness causes the building to twist (torsion) during shaking
Windows on one side break while the other side remains intact

details.summary: Plan irregularity occurs when a building's shape, stiffness distribution, or mass center is asymmetric in plan, causing torsional rotation during earthquakes. Vertical irregularity includes setbacks, soft stories, and mass discontinuities that concentrate damage at transitions.
details.whyItMatters: Irregular buildings experience much worse earthquake performance than regular ones. Asymmetry causes unexpected force concentrations that simple design methods cannot accurately predict.
takeaways: Plan irregularity causes dangerous torsional rotation during lateral shaking
Vertical irregularity concentrates deformation at stiffness discontinuities
Building codes require more rigorous analysis for irregular structures

faq.question: Why does plan asymmetry cause torsion during earthquakes?
faq.answer: When the center of stiffness does not coincide with the center of mass, lateral earthquake forces applied at the center of mass create a twisting moment about the center of stiffness.

faq.question: What are the most dangerous types of vertical irregularity?
faq.answer: Soft stories where stiffness changes abruptly between floors are the most dangerous. Setbacks create stress concentrations at the transition. Mass irregularity from heavy equipment floors concentrates forces at that level.
